questions.prompt: Why do the notes recommend drawing the SR No. in `RowPostPaint` instead of storing it in the row data?
options: Painting is faster than adding a real column, so large grids load much quicker
It is drawn from the row index, so it stays right after inserts, deletes and sorts
Stored SR values cannot be exported to CSV along with the other columns
`RowPostPaint` is the only grid event that fires at all for unbound DataGridViews
questions.explanation: Option A renders `e.RowIndex + 1` while painting, so nothing is kept in the model and the number is always correct after insert/delete/sort/filter. It is the choice when SR is display-only.

source.section: Option A — Best practice: Show SR dynamically (no data change)

questions.prompt: Your SR column must be part of the data because it is exported to CSV. What keeps the numbers correct after the user deletes a row?
options: Nothing extra; the DataGridView renumbers the SR column on its own
Setting `AllowUserToAddRows = false` so the new-row line disappears
Drawing the number in the row header with `TextRenderer.DrawText`
questions.explanation: When SR is a real column (Option B) you must maintain it yourself: `UpdateSerialNumbers()` loops over the rows and sets `Cells["SrColumn"].Value = i + 1`, hooked to `RowsAdded` and `RowsRemoved`.

source.section: Option B — SR is an actual column in grid/data

questions.prompt: `dataGridViewMain.DataSource` is bound to `Program.TransactionData`. Put the steps of the safe way to clear that list in order.
questions.explanation: Clearing the list while it is still bound leaves the grid thinking old rows exist, which leads to an `IndexOutOfRangeException` on repaint. Unbinding first, clearing, then rebinding avoids it.

source.section: ✅ 1. If the List is bound to DataGridView → YES, it WILL cause issues

questions.prompt: In the keyset paging code, which query fetches the next page of `TableTransactions`? (`lastId` holds the last Id of the previous page.)
options: `Where(t => t.Id < lastId).Take(1024)` with no `OrderBy` at all
questions.explanation: Keyset paging relies on a monotonically increasing `Id`: each page asks for rows with `Id > lastId`, ordered by `Id`, and then remembers the last Id it received.

source.section: Keyset paging (RECOMMENDED for large data), for reading records

questions.prompt: According to the notes' comparison table, when is plain `Skip + Take` paging the right choice?
options: For a large table with 10k+ rows
questions.explanation: The table recommends `Skip + Take` only for a small table; large tables, continuous scrolling and stable sorting all call for keyset paging.
